messages.subject: Re: levels/groups on axis strings
parts:
Hi:

Here's one way, but it may not be what you want aesthetically. The idea is to create sub-panels for the nested levels.

*Reproducible example*   (!!!)

dd <- data.frame(fac1 = factor(rep(c("I", "II", "III"), each = 60)),
                  fac2 = factor(rep(c("A", "B"), c(40, 20))),
                  fac3 = factor(rep(letters[1:3], each = 20)),
                  fac4 = factor(rep(c("w1", "w2"), each = 10)),
                     y = rnorm(180))

ggplot(dd, aes(x = fac3, y = y, color = fac4)) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.1)) +
    facet_grid(. ~ fac1 + fac2, scales = "free_x")

I'd prefer to visualize the nesting of fac2 within fac1 by having a solid fac1 level strip across all levels of fac2, but AFAIK that isn't implemented in ggplot2 at present.              

Dennis

The only way I know its using grid.text but is very hard to use.

messages.subject: Re: levels/groups on axis strings
parts:
Hi:

You could open an issue at https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues and make it clear that your wishlist item has to do with nested sets of factor levels. If it's possible to extend the formula notation to embrace nested factors, e.g., facet_wrap( ~ A/B) [B nested within A], that would be even better, but I imagine that some parts of the code might break with such an extension. Just a thought....

Dennis
